BBC News live page. LD datePublished 15 Oct 07:54 BST. WARNING: one LD dateModified reads 2026-10-16T13:39:00.000Z - a FUTURE date, clearly a bad stamp; do not use it. Live page 'Updated' counter was running at time of capture.
Headline: 'Pakistan school roof collapse: At least 28 killed as rescuers search for survivors'.
TOLL IS MOVING - DOCUMENTED IN-PAGE WITHIN TEN MINUTES. Attribute as of a stated time:
- 08:26 BST entry ('What we do and don't know'): 'At least 19 people - including 18 children - have been killed in a roof collapse at a school in Peshawar - the capital of Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.'
- 08:36 BST entry, marked Breaking, by Usman Zahid reporting from Islamabad: 'At least 28 people, including 27 students and one teacher, have been killed after the roof of a school collapsed in Peshawar, Pakistan, Lady Reading Hospital spokesperson Mohammad Asim tells the BBC.'
Mohammad Asim, spokesperson for Peshawar's Lady Reading Hospital: 19 others injured, including five in a critical condition. Most of the children sustained head injuries. Children aged between 6 and 12. Many parents have arrived at the hospital and the administration has sought police assistance to control the crowd.
Rescue teams searching the rubble for survivors, with more children feared trapped.
Ishaq Dar, Pakistan's deputy prime minister, in a post on X: the collapse has 'deeply pained the entire nation'. 'Our children are our most precious asset, and every such loss is a tragedy for the entire country.' Dar said the prime minister and government have taken serious note, and the safety and protection of children 'must remain paramount'. 'All necessary measures must be taken to provide immediate assistance to those affected, ensure the best possible medical care for the injured, and strengthen safety standards in our schools to prevent such tragedies from recurring.'
Location: Peshawar, capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.
Agency tokens: Reuters (image source credit on the Peshawar crowd photo - photo credit only).
NOTE: the brief's figure of 27 came from a blocked outlet; BBC has 28 (27 students + 1 teacher) and the toll was still rising.
